subject: government
topic: Basic concepts: power, authority, legitimacy and sovereignty

kept.q: In Government, 'power' is best defined as:
options: the legal right to rule a state
the ability to influence or control the behaviour of others, even against their will
the recognition given to a ruler by his people
the supreme authority of a state over its territory
kept.explanation: Power is the capacity to make people act in a certain way, whether they agree or not. It does not need to be legal or accepted to exist, unlike authority or legitimacy.
kept.pidgin: Power na the fit to make people do wetin you want, even if dem no agree. E no need to be legal or dem to accept am before e dey there.

kept.q: Authority is different from mere power mainly because authority:
options: is always backed by military force
is the legitimate right to exercise power and command obedience
cannot be challenged by any citizen
exists only in a democratic system of government
kept.explanation: Authority is power that is recognised as lawful or rightful. A person in authority is obeyed because people accept his right to command, not just because he can force them.
kept.pidgin: Authority na power wey people accept say e correct. Dem dey obey the person because dem believe say e get the right to command, no be say na only force e dey use.

options: the ability to use force to control citizens
the general acceptance by the people that a government has the right to rule
the independence of a state from foreign control
the power to make laws for a country
kept.explanation: Legitimacy means the people see a government's rule as rightful and proper, usually because it followed accepted rules like free elections or tradition.
kept.pidgin: Legitimacy na when the citizens agree say the government get correct right to dey rule, mostly because the government follow accepted process like free election.

kept.q: Sovereignty, as used in Government studies, is best described as:
options: the supreme and final authority within a state
the right of citizens to vote during elections
the ability of a government to collect taxes from citizens
the influence a leader has over members of his cabinet
kept.explanation: Sovereignty is the highest and final authority in a state, above which there is no other power, either inside the country or from outside, that the state must obey.
kept.pidgin: Sovereignty na the highest and final power for inside one state, no other power — whether from inside or outside — fit control am.

kept.q: Which situation best illustrates the external sovereignty of Nigeria as a state?
options: The National Assembly making laws for the whole federation
Nigeria's independence from control by Britain or any other foreign power
The President appointing ministers to head government ministries
The judiciary interpreting the provisions of the 1999 Constitution
kept.explanation: External sovereignty means a state is free from control by any outside power and relates freely with other nations as an equal. Nigeria's independence from Britain shows this freedom from foreign control.
kept.pidgin: External sovereignty mean say no foreign country fit control the state again. Nigeria wey don free from Britain control na clear example of external sovereignty.

kept.q: A state's internal sovereignty is shown when the government:
options: signs a trade treaty with another country
exercises supreme authority over all persons and groups within its own territory
joins an international body like the African Union
receives diplomatic recognition from other nations
kept.explanation: Internal sovereignty concerns supreme control inside the state itself, over all citizens, institutions and groups within its borders. Treaties and recognition deal with external sovereignty, not internal.
kept.pidgin: Internal sovereignty na when government get final power for inside im own territory, over all the people and groups dem. Treaty and recognition na external sovereignty matter.

kept.q: Major Danjuma took over the government of a fictional West African country through a military coup. He fully controls the armed forces and can enforce his orders, but most citizens see his government as unlawful and refuse to cooperate with it. This situation best shows that Major Danjuma has:
options: power without legitimacy
authority without power
sovereignty without authority
legitimacy without power
kept.explanation: Danjuma can force obedience (power) because he controls the army, but the people do not accept his rule as rightful, so he lacks legitimacy. This is a classic case of power without legitimacy.
kept.pidgin: Danjuma get the army so e fit force people to obey am — na power. But the citizens no gree say im rule correct, so e no get legitimacy. Na power without legitimacy be dis.

kept.q: In a certain country, the constitution clearly states that the National Assembly holds supreme law-making power. In practice, however, powerful political godfathers and pressure groups actually decide most government policies behind the scenes. This situation best illustrates the difference between:
options: internal sovereignty and external sovereignty
legal sovereignty and political sovereignty
power and legitimacy
de jure government and de facto government
kept.explanation: Legal sovereignty is the authority officially recognised by the constitution or law (the National Assembly). Political sovereignty is the real, actual power behind government decisions (the godfathers/pressure groups), which may differ from who holds power on paper.
kept.pidgin: Legal sovereignty na the power wey constitution talk say National Assembly get on paper. Political sovereignty na the real power wey dey behind the scene — for dis case na the godfathers and pressure groups. Na so e different be dis.
